request: Battery Consumed Columns - Vehicle Snapshots (MAG-10). Add derived columns to vehicle_snapshots computed from the current row and the previous record for that vehicle: distance traveled (odometer delta), battery consumed (battery_level_pct delta, may be negative), km per 1% battery, and estimated range (km_per_pct x 100). Suffix every new column with 'calc'. Calculate them before saving the nightly gathered data. 'Yesterday' means the latest record tracked for that vehicle. Ticket also asks whether the formulas can be applied to existing database records.

review.brief: Review the whole branch diff (main..HEAD, 5 commits: 03daca4, 98d1358, 9325b4c, 0101ad3, b1a8d2b) for the change telemetry-add-derived-consumption-columns. Validate, in priority order: (1) DESIGN-GATE FIDELITY - every DB object must match the design the user confirmed at the gate (D7): exactly five nullable columns with the design.md names/types, no sixth column, NO NEW INDEX, and the in-migration LAG() backfill. Any mismatch is a BLOCKER finding. (2) FORMULA AGREEMENT - the migration's SQL backfill and Go's deriveConsumption must produce identical values for the same inputs: same subtraction order, same '> 0' divisor guard, same x100 range, same whole-day count. A divergence would silently split backfilled history from newly written rows - treat as blocker. (3) D2/DU2 NULL semantics - km_per_pct_calc and estimated_range_km_calc NULL iff battery_used_pct_calc <= 0, while the raw columns always keep the true signed delta including negatives; a stored zero must stay truthful and never be clamped to NULL. (4) D6/D7 SAME-DAY RECAPTURE - InsertVehicleSnapshot's ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET must refresh all five columns, and the predecessor bound must be the LOCAL calendar-day start, never the incoming row's own captured_at. (5) ERROR CONTAINMENT - a previousSnapshot query failure must never be mistakable for 'no predecessor'; confirm it routes through logAPIError as ReasonAPIError and cannot NULL out a real vehicle's columns on a transient DB hiccup. (6) BOUNDARIES (V10) - internal/telemetry imports only account + tesla public packages; pgtype appears in no public type or interface; no file outside internal/telemetry was touched; gateway-battery-consumed-chart was not referenced (D5). (7) PERFORMANCE-PROFILE - read-heavy: values are precomputed on the write path and never derived on read; PreviousSnapshotForVehicle rides the existing idx_vehicle_snapshots_vehicle_time as a backward scan. (8) CONVENTIONS - the km/degC/PSI display-unit suffix rule, helper reuse (no new pgtype or mapping helper was to be written - verify none was), and doc accuracy in internal/telemetry/AGENTS.md. (9) ANTI-GAMING - no task title, acceptance criterion or test was weakened, simplified or deleted; tasks.md checkboxes match reality. TWO LEADER-DISCLOSED ITEMS TO SCRUTINIZE RATHER THAN ASSUME: (a) D14 is a USER-APPROVED SCOPE EXPANSION outside tasks.md - testdb_test.go's TestMain now logs+continues instead of log.Fatalf, and newTestStore t.Skip's instead of t.Fatalf. Judge whether it is implemented safely and whether the AGENTS.md documentation of it is adequate; it being user-approved is not a reason to skip judging its implementation. (b) D15 is a leader integration fix reading the clock once in attemptVehicle. THE MOST IMPORTANT LIMITATION: T7 is BLOCKED - its three DB integration tests (including TestStore_SnapshotUpsert_RecapturesRecomputeDerivedColumns, the regression for the D6/D7 staleness fix) are written and type-check but have NEVER EXECUTED, because Docker is unavailable (D13). The migration and its backfill have never run against a real Postgres either. The user has explicitly accepted proceeding to review with this gap and will run the DB tests afterwards. Do NOT treat the DB layer as proven, and do NOT ask for the tests to be run - instead review that unexecuted test code especially carefully by reading it, since nothing else will catch a mistake in it before the user runs it. Read the diff, not the whole module. Escalate on doubt: return changes-requested rather than approving anything you are unsure of.

findings.note: internal/testdb/testdb.go Provision() + internal/telemetry/testdb_test.go:52-59 (D14): a container-provisioning failure (no Docker) and a migration-application failure (goose up / this migration is broken) both return the same generic error from Provision, and TestMain treats them identically - log.Printf + continue. decisions.decision: Multi-day gaps store the RAW delta plus a new days_spanned_calc column (five columns, not four)
decisions.why: Preserves the true total while keeping the gap visible; averaging per-day would destroy the real figure irrecoverably, and a bare raw delta would make a 2-day bar indistinguishable from a 1-day one

decisions.decision: km_per_pct_calc and estimated_range_km_calc are NULL whenever battery_used_pct_calc <= 0; the two raw columns always store the true signed delta
decisions.why: Zero divisor is a division by zero and a negative divisor (overnight charge) yields a meaningless ratio; module convention D12/DSA3 reserves NULL for genuinely undefined and requires a stored 0 to be truthful

decisions.decision: Column naming is <what>_<unit>_calc; ticket's estimated_range_calculated becomes estimated_range_km_calc
decisions.why: Honors both the ticket's requested _calc suffix and CLAUDE.md's non-negotiable display-unit suffix rule, matching the 15 existing unit-suffixed columns on the table

decisions.decision: Accepted the worker's refinement of the previous-record definition: bound the lookup by the start of the incoming row's LOCAL CALENDAR DAY, not by its own captured_at
